pitch: A Gateway between any AI Agent and its MCP servers. Every Tool call gets a Decision: allow, redact, hold or deny.

v1.item: Public demo deployed, with request limits
README: pitch, demo link, eval table

components.name: 6 fake bank servers
components.note: accounts, transactions, payments, tickets, notify, fx-rates

eval.note: Committed runs only. Confused-deputy Attacks already fail with defences off, so the v1 defences must prove themselves on exfiltration, tool poisoning and rug pull.

tickets.title: Design docs before code
tickets.how: One term per concept, words to avoid listed.
tickets.why: Fixed vocabulary keeps issues, code and UI consistent.

tickets.title: Gateway as an MCP proxy
tickets.what: Gateway is one MCP server; real servers sit behind it.
tickets.how: Servers run as child processes over stdio, no network port.
tickets.why: One boundary the Agent cannot skip; any MCP client is protected.
tickets.rejected: Library inside the Agent (bypassable); raw HTTP proxy (cannot see tool names).

tickets.title: Cedar permissions
tickets.what: Every Tool call decided by person, role, tool, arguments.
tickets.how: Policy files validated against a schema at startup.
tickets.why: Default-deny and reviewable: a tool with no rule is denied.

tickets.title: Hash-chained Audit log
tickets.what: Every Decision written to an Audit log Supervisors verify.
tickets.how: Each entry carries the hash of the one before.
tickets.why: Editing an old entry breaks the chain, so tampering shows.

tickets.title: Red-team eval harness
tickets.what: Attacks and Benign tasks run with defences off and on.
tickets.how: Fresh bank and Gateway per task; Canaries prove exfiltration.
tickets.why: Measured, not claimed: Attack success rate next to False block rate.

tickets.title: Flow strip
tickets.what: Each Tool call shown travelling Agent → Gateway → server.
tickets.how: Real Audit entries over Server-Sent Events.
tickets.why: A recruiter sees an attack stopped in 30 seconds.

concepts.name: Policy boundary outside the Agent
concepts.plain: Security checks live in a process the model cannot change.
concepts.tradeoff: Extra hop and latency, but works for any MCP client.
concepts.q: Why not enforce rules in the system prompt?
concepts.a: Injected text can override a prompt; the Gateway checks each Tool call in code.

concepts.name: Default-deny authorization
concepts.plain: Anything not explicitly allowed is refused.
concepts.tradeoff: Safer, but every new tool needs a rule before it works.
concepts.q: What happens to a new tool with no policy?
concepts.a: Cedar denies it until a policy permits it.

concepts.name: Token audience
concepts.plain: A token says which service it is for; others reject it.
concepts.tradeoff: Two tokens to manage, but a hijacked Agent cannot use UI endpoints.
concepts.q: Why give the Agent and the UI different tokens?
concepts.a: So a stolen MCP token cannot call UI endpoints, and the reverse.

concepts.name: Canary
concepts.plain: A unique fake value whose appearance outside proves a leak.
concepts.tradeoff: Exact and cheap to check; only catches leaks of planted values.
concepts.q: How does the eval know exfiltration worked?
concepts.a: A Canary shows up in what notify or fx-rates received.
